recipes.title: Chinese steamed eggs with shrimp, light
recipes.summary: Silky steamed eggs with tender shrimp and shiitake mushrooms, served with a modest portion of rice. The protein stays generous while the starch and sesame oil remain light.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Prepare the shrimp, shiitake mushrooms, spring onions and ginger in their listed forms.
Whisk the eggs until the whites and yolks are evenly combined.
Stir the chicken broth and soy sauce into the eggs without creating too much foam.
Arrange the shrimp and shiitake mushrooms in a shallow heatproof bowl.
Pour the egg mixture over the shrimp and mushrooms.
Steam the eggs gently until the centre is softly set and the shrimp are opaque.
Rest the steamed eggs so the custard finishes setting.
Finish with the sesame oil, spring onions and ginger, then serve with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served immediately while the custard is silky. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat very gently. Store the rice separately. Freezing is not recommended.

Finish with the sesame oil, spring onions and ginger, then serve with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served immediately while the custard is silky. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat very gently. Store the rice separately. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Chinese steamed eggs with shrimp, hearty

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep the larger portion covered so it finishes steaming evenly.

Whisk the eggs until the whites and yolks are evenly combined.
Stir the chicken broth and soy sauce into the eggs until smooth.

recipes.title: Provençal cod and vegetables, light
recipes.summary: Cod baked over zucchini, peppers, potatoes and tomatoes with garlic, thyme, basil and lemon. Extra vegetables and less oil keep this Provençal lunch light and Mediterranean.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the cod, potato, zucchini, bell pepper, onion, garlic and basil in their listed forms.
Coat the potato and onion with half the olive oil and half the thyme.
Roast the potato and onion until they begin to soften and colour.
Add the zucchini and bell pepper to the roasting dish.
Pour the tomatoes, canned, around the vegetables.
Scatter the garlic and remaining thyme over the vegetables.
Roast the vegetables until the zucchini is tender and the tomato sauce has reduced slightly.
Place the cod over the vegetables and brush it with the remaining olive oil.
Bake until the cod is opaque and flakes easily at the thickest point.
Finish the Provençal cod with the basil and lemon juice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat covered until the cod is hot. The vegetables keep well, but the fish is best fresh. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Greek stuffed peppers, light
recipes.summary: Bell peppers baked with a savoury filling of beef, rice, zucchini, tomatoes, dill and thyme. Extra vegetables and less rice and oil keep this Mediterranean dinner lighter.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Prepare the bell pepper, zucchini, onion and garlic in their listed forms.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Heat half the olive oil in a wide frying pan.
Brown the ground beef until no pink remains.
Cook the onion and zucchini until softened and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, dill weed and thyme and stir until fragrant.
Stir the white rice and tomatoes, canned, into the beef mixture.
Pour in half the vegetable broth and simmer until the rice begins to soften.
Arrange the bell pepper halves in a baking dish and brush them with the remaining olive oil.
Fill the bell pepper with the beef and rice mixture.
Pour the remaining vegetable broth around the stuffed peppers.
Cover and bake until the peppers are tender and the rice is cooked through.
Uncover and bake until the tops are lightly browned.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until steaming. Freeze cooked stuffed peppers for up to 2 months and thaw overnight before reheating.

recipes.title: Greek stuffed peppers, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous tray of Greek stuffed peppers with extra beef and rice in a rich tomato, dill and thyme filling. It is a substantial Mediterranean dinner for four.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Prepare the bell pepper, zucchini, onion and garlic in their listed forms.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Heat half the olive oil in a large frying pan.
Brown the ground beef in batches until deeply coloured.
Cook the onion and zucchini until completely softened.
Add the garlic, dill weed and thyme and stir until fragrant.
Stir the white rice and tomatoes, canned, into the beef mixture.
Pour in half the vegetable broth and simmer until the rice begins to soften.
Arrange the bell pepper halves across two baking dishes and brush them with the remaining olive oil.
Fill the bell pepper generously with the beef and rice mixture.
Pour the remaining vegetable broth around the stuffed peppers.
Cover and bake until the peppers are very tender and the rice is fully cooked.
Uncover and bake until the tops are browned.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until steaming. Freeze cooked stuffed peppers for up to 2 months and thaw overnight before reheating.

recipes.title: Moroccan harira, light
recipes.summary: A lighter vegan Moroccan harira with red lentils, chickpeas, tomatoes, vegetables and warming ginger and cumin. Extra broth and vegetables keep the breakfast filling but not heavy.

steps.instruction: Rinse the red lentils under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Prepare the onion, carrot, celery, garlic, ginger and cilantro in their listed forms.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery until softened and fragrant.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, vegetable broth and red lentils.
Simmer the harira until the red lentils are tender and beginning to thicken the broth.
Stir in the chickpeas, canned, and simmer until hot and tender.
Fold the cilantro and lemon juice through the harira.
Rest the Moroccan harira briefly before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat with extra vegetable broth if needed. The harira freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Spanish chickpea and spinach stew, light
recipes.summary: An Andalusian-style stew of chickpeas and spinach thickened with toasted bread, garlic, tomato, cumin and paprika. Extra spinach and less bread and oil keep it light.

steps.instruction: Prepare the bread, onion and garlic in their listed forms.
Heat half the olive oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat.
Toast the bread until crisp and golden on both sides.
Transfer the bread to a food processor.
Cook the onion in the remaining olive oil until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and simmer until thickened slightly.
Blend the toasted bread with the tomato mixture and vegetable broth into a coarse sauce.
Return the sauce to the pan and stir in the chickpeas, canned.
Simmer the chickpeas until hot and coated in the thick sauce.
Fold in the spinach and cook until wilted and tender.
Finish the Spanish chickpea and spinach stew with the lemon juice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat gently with a splash of vegetable broth. Freeze for up to 2 months, though the spinach will soften.
